Last updated November 14, 2026.

Michigan property tax is set locally, and owners can appeal to the March board of review and then the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

What the official sources say

  • Board of review meets the second Monday in March; a city or township may authorize alternative start dates of the Tuesday or Wednesday following. (MCL 211.30; source)
  • Tax Tribunal petition deadline: May 31 of the tax year for commercial, industrial, developmental real property and commercial/industrial/utility personal property. (MCL 205.735a(6); source)
  • Tax Tribunal petition deadline: July 31 of the tax year for agricultural, residential, timber-cutover real property and agricultural personal property. (MCL 205.735a(6); source)
  • In all other tribunal matters, a petition must be filed within 35 days after the final decision, ruling, or determination. (MCL 205.735a(6); source)
  • Taxable value is the lesser of (a) prior-year taxable value minus losses times the lesser of 1.05 or the inflation rate, plus additions, or (b) current state equalized valuation (Proposal A cap). (MCL 211.27a(2); source)
  • On a transfer of ownership, taxable value for the following calendar year becomes the property's state equalized valuation (uncapping). (MCL 211.27a(3); source)
  • The buyer must notify the local assessing office of the transfer within 45 days on a State Tax Commission form (Property Transfer Affidavit). (MCL 211.27a; source)
  • Form 2766 Property Transfer Affidavit must be filed by the new owner with the city/township assessor within 45 days of transfer. (Treasury Form 2766, Property Transfer Affidavit; source)
  • On March 1, property delinquent for taxes, interest, penalties and fees for the preceding 12 months or more is forfeited to the county treasurer. (MCL 211.78g(1); source)
  • Within 45 days of forfeiture the county treasurer records a certificate with the register of deeds. (MCL 211.78g(2); source)
  • Forfeited property may be redeemed on or before the March 31 following entry of the foreclosure judgment (or within 21 days after judgment in a contested case) by paying all amounts due. (MCL 211.78g(3); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Michigan exempts a principal residence from the local school operating tax if the owner files the affidavit.

What the official sources say

  • A principal residence is exempt from the tax levied by a local school district for school operating purposes if the owner files an affidavit. (MCL 211.7cc(1); source)
  • For taxes levied after 2011, the affidavit is due on or before June 1 for the summer levy or on or before November 1 for the winter levy. (MCL 211.7cc(2); source)
  • The exemption lasts until December 31 of the year the property is transferred or is no longer a principal residence. (MCL 211.7cc(4); source)
  • An owner must rescind the exemption within 90 days after the property stops being the owner's principal residence; late rescission penalty is $5 per day up to $200. (MCL 211.7cc(5); source)
  • An owner may retain the exemption up to 3 tax years on a former residence if it is not occupied, is for sale, not leased, and not used for business, by filing a conditional rescission form. (MCL 211.7cc(5); source)
  • Form 2368 Principal Residence Exemption Affidavit is filed with the city/township assessor; deadlines June 1 (summer levy) and November 1 (winter levy). (Treasury: PRE Claim Requirement; source)
  • A principal residence exemption exempts the home from local school operating millage, up to 18 mills. (Treasury: Principal Residence Exemption; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Michigan charges both a state and a county real estate transfer tax on deeds.

What the official sources say

  • State real estate transfer tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of the total value of property transferred. (MCL 207.525(1); source)
  • County real estate transfer tax is 55 cents per $500 in counties under 2,000,000 population; up to 75 cents per $500 in counties of 2,000,000 or more. (MCL 207.504; source)
  • State transfer tax exempt: instruments with consideration under $100. (MCL 207.526(a); source)
  • State transfer tax exempt: conveyance from an individual to the individual's child, stepchild, adopted child, or grandchild. (MCL 207.526(j),(k); source)
  • State transfer tax exempt: instruments transferring property pursuant to or in lieu of mortgage foreclosure (not a subsequent transfer by the foreclosing entity). (MCL 207.526(v); source)
  • State transfer tax exempt: quitclaim deed to confirm title already vested/correct a flaw in title; judgments/orders of a court of record without specified monetary consideration. (MCL 207.526(l),(n); source)
  • County transfer tax exemptions include consideration under $100, leases, security instruments, court orders, boundary line instruments, and land contracts where legal title has not passed. (MCL 207.505; source)
  • State transfer tax is $3.75 per $500; county tax is $0.55 per $500 (up to $0.75 in counties of 2,000,000+). (MCL 207.525; MCL 207.504; source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee is $30 per document. (MCL 600.2567; source)

Michigan evictions are summary proceedings in district court.

What the official sources say

  • Summary proceedings may be used to recover possession when a tenant holds over after failing to pay rent within 7 days of a written demand for possession. (MCL 600.5714(1)(a); source)

  • For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may terminate the tenancy with a written 7-day notice to quit. (MCL 554.134(2); source)
  • A tenancy from year to year may be terminated by either party by notice to quit. (MCL 554.134(3); source)
  • Summary proceedings remedy is in addition to other remedies; judgment for possession does not bar other claims except as stated for land contract forfeiture. (MCL 600.5750; source)
  • A tenant holding over after termination of the lease under the lease or by law is subject to summary proceedings. (MCL 600.5714(1)(c)(i); source)
  • A written 7-day notice to quit may be used for nonpayment of rent. (MCL 554.134(2); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

A Michigan quitclaim deed is recorded with the register of deeds, and some transfers are exempt from transfer tax.

What the official sources say

  • A conveyance worded 'A.B. quit claims to C.D.' (premises, consideration), signed, sealed and acknowledged by the grantor, is a sufficient quitclaim conveyance. (MCL 565.152; source)
  • Transfer tax exempt: quitclaim deed to confirm title already vested or correct a flaw in title. (MCL 207.526(n); source)
  • Conveyance from an individual to child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild is exempt from state transfer tax. (MCL 207.526(j),(k); source)
  • Register of deeds fee for entering and recording a document is $30 regardless of page count. (MCL 600.2567(1)(a); source)
  • Copies of records are $1.00 per page. (MCL 600.2567(1)(c); source)
  • Electronic documents under the Uniform Real Property Electronic Recording Act may be recorded where the register accepts them; electronic fee is due within 1 business day of receipt. (MCL 600.2567; source)
  • Recordable instruments must show each executing person's printed name beneath the signature, be legible, black ink on white paper, 8-1/2 by 11 to 8-1/2 by 14 inches, with a 2-1/2 inch top margin on page 1 and 1/2 inch margins elsewhere. (MCL 565.201; source)
